title: Traffic policy schema, validator & rollout strategy (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a traffic policy schema (JSON), a lightweight validator we can run in the control plane, and the rollout mechanics (canary -> ramp -> fallback) for multi-region routing policies. Goal is to standardize: policy shape, basic static validation, runtime semantic checks, rollout automation, and observability / rollback triggers.

Context / goals (quick):
- Platform needs one canonical policy format used by hosted + dedicated control planes.
- Policies describe routing by model family, model variant, capacity tier, region preferences, fallback chains, and cost-latency tradeoffs.
- Validator must catch obvious misconfigs before apply (missing required fields, invalid region codes, incompatible model pairings).
- Rollouts should be safe: small canary, automated metric-based ramp, automatic fallback to last good known policy if regressions detected.

High-level requirements:
- Human-editable JSON/YAML; small schema surface.
- Backwards compatible: schema v1 with opt-in v1.1 fields.
- Declarative: state describes desired routing behavior; controller handles orchestration.
- Short-circuit safe defaults: if policy references unknown model, reject apply; if region unreachable, route to next tier.
- Audit-friendly: every apply creates a transaction id and stores previous policy snapshot.

Proposed JSON schema (informal):
{
  "schema_version": "string, e.g. \"redwood-routing.v1\"",
  "policy_id": "string (slug)",
  "description": "string",
  "match": [
    {
      "predicate": "object (type: client_attr / route_name / header / regex)",
      "priority": "integer (higher wins)"
    }
  ],
  "routes": [
    {
      "route_id": "string",
      "targets": [
        {
          "model": "string (model-id or alias)",
          "variant": "string? (e.g. fp16-qat)",
          "weight": "int (0-100, relative)",
          "region_affinity": ["string region codes"],
          "capacity_tier": "string (on-demand|reserved|burst)",
          "constraints": {"max_latency_ms": "int (optional)", "max_cost_per_token": "float (optional)"}
        }
      ],
      "fallback_chain": ["route_id"]
    }
  ],
  "deployment": {
    "rollout": {
      "strategy": "canary|linear|manual",
      "canary": {"size_pct": "int","duration_minutes": "int"},
      "ramp": {"step_minutes": "int","step_increment_pct": "int"},
      "health_check": {
         "metrics": ["latency_p50","error_rate","quality_regression_score"],
         "slo_thresholds": {"latency_p50_ms": "int","error_rate_pct": "float"},
         "rollback_on": "string (any|all)"
      }
    },
    "dry_run": "bool (if true, no traffic moved)"
  },
  "metadata": {"author":"string","created_at":"iso-date","tags":["strings"]}
}

Notes on schema choices:
- Use weight-based targets per route to express probabilistic split (sum weights normalized).
- region_affinity is *preference* not strict; runtime may still route elsewhere if unavailable. Provide allow_fallback boolean if strictly required.
- capacity_tier distinguishes reserved/dedicated capacity from burst/hosted so controller can honor SLAs.
- health checks include both infra (latency, errors) and quality signals (eval-set regressions or sampling-based fuzzy match).

Validator design (control plane pre-flight):
1) Static validation (fast): JSON schema validate + custom rules: unique route_ids, weights sum > 0 for route, region codes are known, model ids exist in internal catalog (or warning if alias), no circular fallback chains.
2) Semantic checks (requires quick control plane lookups): check model compatibility (e.g., model A quantized variant not compatible with KV cache path expected by client). If check cannot be completed fast, mark as "needs_manual_review" but allow a dry_run.
3) Risk scoring: compute a score (0-100) based on: #regions changed, model family changed, weight shifted > X%, targets added/removed, use of non-dedicated capacity for critical routes. This score drives default rollout strategy (e.g. score>70 -> manual approval).
4) Linting hints: suggest adding a canary section if policy touches production routes.

Validator outputs (structured list):
- status: pass|warn|fail|needs_manual_review
- issues: ["string messages"]
- suggested_rollout_profile: "low|medium|high"
- transaction_id: "uuid"
- snapshot_url: "internal store link"

Rollout mechanics (controller behavior):
- Apply API receives policy + requestor + dry_run flag.
- On apply: create transaction snapshot, run validator. If fail -> reject. If warn/needs_manual_review -> send to approvers (configured per team).
- If approved or low risk: kick off rollout controller.

Canary flow (automated):
1) Start canary: move traffic for specified percentage to route targets in target region(s). Label canary traffic with transaction id.
2) Observe health window (canary.duration). Collect infra + quality metrics.
3) Evaluate: if any metric breaches thresholds -> initiate immediate rollback to previous snapshot.
4) If canary ok -> ramp according to ramp.step_minutes and step_increment_pct until target weights fulfilled.
5) Finalize: mark transaction state=active, record audit.

Rollback behaviors:
- Immediate rollback: revert to previous policy snapshot across all regions. Create rollback transaction with parent id.
- Partial rollback: if issue localized to region/variant, controller can shrink or remove offending target and continue ramp elsewhere.
- Forced fallback: policy-level fallback_chain should be used to reroute requests to pre-declared safe targets if primary target fails at runtime.

Observability and metrics (must be emitted per transaction):
- per-transaction traffic volume, error_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost_per_token estimate, sampled-output-quality (fuzzy similarity to reference), SLA_breaches count, region_miss_routing_count.
- tracing: span includes policy.transaction_id and route_id so we can aggregate by policy.
- dashboard: quick view for active transactions with green/yellow/red UX.

Testing and canary verification:
- Local integration harness: simulates traffic mix (prompt length dist, session affinity) and asserts policy splits are honored.
- Golden-match tests: sample outputs from canary targets evaluated by prompt set to detect quality regressions.
- Chaos tests: simulate regional outage to ensure fallback chain semantics behave as expected.

Edge cases and unresolved questions (TODOs):
- How to express "cost cap per request" that applies across targets with different per-token costs? (we can approximate with avg cost buckets and drop targets exceeding cap)
- Should we support weighted routing by latency SLA instead of simple weights? (i.e., route requests under latency-sensitivity bucket differently)
- How to express time-bounded rules (e.g., route X only between 00:00-06:00 UTC)? Add schedule object?
- How to model sticky session affinity across multi-region replica sets?

Operational playbook (short):
- Default policy lifecycle: draft -> validator pass -> canary auto (2% for 30m) -> ramp (2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
- If validator risk score >= 70 -> require manual approval by eng-platform + owning product.
- Metrics to watch during rollout: error_rate (alert if > baseline + 3x stddev or absolute > 1%), latency_p95 (alert if +20% vs baseline), sampled-output-quality (alert if regression > configured delta).
- Rollback steps: controller auto-revert OR ops run `platformctl revert --tx <id>`. Postmortem required for auto-rollback incidents.

Implementation notes (pragmatic):
- Start with server-side JSON schema + a node/python-based validator service. Keep validation idempotent and fast (<200ms target).
- Integrate with existing config-store (etcd/raft) with transactional apply. Store snapshots in S3 for audit.
- Expose dry_run and lint endpoints in control plane UI.
- Hook into existing observability (console) with transaction-scoped dashboards.

Example minimal policy (JSON):
{
  "schema_version": "redwood-routing.v1",
  "policy_id": "chatbot-main-aug-2026",
  "description": "Route chat completion traffic: prefer low-cost fp16, fallback to large-llm in eu if latency spikes",
  "match": [{"predicate": {"route_name": "/chat/completions"}, "priority": 10}],
  "routes": [{
     "route_id": "main",
     "targets": [
       {"model": "gptx-fp16", "weight": 80, "region_affinity": ["us-west1"], "capacity_tier": "reserved"},
       {"model": "gptx-large", "weight": 20, "region_affinity": ["us-west1", "eu-west1"], "capacity_tier": "on-demand"}
     ],
     "fallback_chain": ["safe-fallback"]
  }],
  "deployment": {
    "rollout": {
      "strategy": "canary",
      "canary": {"size_pct": 2, "duration_minutes": 30},
      "ramp": {"step_minutes": 15, "step_increment_pct": 8},
      "health_check": {"metrics": ["error_rate","latency_p95"], "slo_thresholds": {"error_rate_pct": 0.5, "latency_p95_ms": 1200}, "rollback_on": "any"}
    },
    "dry_run": false
  },
  "metadata": {"author": "Maya Patel", "created_at": "2025-11-20T14:00:00Z", "tags": ["chat","critical"]}
}

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally opinionated about canary sizes (small default) and validator risk scoring. Need feedback on thresholds and whether product should be able to override.
- I think we should prototype validator + simple controller in the platform repo, then migrate to the control plane service.

Quick checklist before merge:
- [ ] Add JSON Schema file to repo (schema/redwood-routing.v1.json)
- [ ] Add unit tests for validator rules (unique routes, fallback loops)
- [ ] Wire model catalog lookup for semantic checks
- [ ] Add transaction audit view to Console prototype
- [ ] Draft runbook for manual approval flow

End of sketch.
